text:
anya: Quick sync — we need a clear split for post-launch work. Proposing: critical customer-impacting issues (crashes, data loss, major workflow block) go into a 1.0.1 hotfix; everything else (UX polish, performance tweaks, small feature gaps) goes into 1.1. Thoughts? @michael @sam

michael: I like that. Two small asks: 1) define what "major workflow block" means (how many users / severity), 2) cutoff for hotfix inclusion (we need a hard deadline).

sam: Agree. For severity, suggest: "blocks primary user path for >=5% DAU or any paying customer blocking signup/checkout". For cutoff: 48h before QA freeze for hotfix.

jordan: 48h seems tight if we need investigation. Can we do 72h for non-crash issues, keep 48h for regressions/crashes? Also need an ETA for engineering capacity — how many devs can pick up hotfix?

lee: We can reallocate 2 devs + 1 on-call SRE next week for the hotfix window. Suggest we maintain a short triage board and a single assignee per bug to keep momentum. Also: telemetry runbook must be updated so we can roll back if perf regresses.

anya: Good catches. Updated proposal:
- Hotfix (1.0.1) inclusion criteria:
  - Crashes / data loss -> always hotfix
  - Regressions impacting core flow and >=5% DAU or blocking any paid customer -> hotfix
  - Security or compliance issues -> hotfix
- Cutoffs:
  - Regressions/crashes/security: up to 48h before deploy window
  - Non-crash but blocking core flow: up to 72h before deploy window
- Capacity: 2 devs + 1 SRE reserved.

Please review the quick triage rubric below and drop a +1 or suggestions. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll lock the schedule and publish to customers.

```
Triage rubric (quick):
- Severity: Crash/data loss (P0), Blocker core flow (P0/P1), Degradation (P1), Minor UX/perf (P2)
- Customer signal: Paying customer blocked (escalate), >5% DAU affected (escalate)
- Repro: deterministic > flaky
- Suggested owner: team owning the failing workflow
```

michael: +1 to the rubric. Suggest adding a field for "risk of fix" (high/medium/low) so we can decide if a patch needs extra QA.

sam: +1. Also, let's batch small low-risk fixes into a single hotfix chunk to reduce churn — group by owner and area.

anya: Noted. I'll add "risk_of_fix" to the rubric and create a short board in the console (flag: postlaunch-hotfix) for items. Can someone on ENG create the board and link? @sam?

sam: I'll create it now and link in this thread when ready. ETA 30m.

ops-bot: Deploy window for next hotfix candidates is scheduled for 2024-05-10T02:00:00Z. Please ensure items are triaged and assigned before cutoff.

jordan: Thanks — that gives us time. If anyone hears from customers with urgent issues, ping me and I'll escalate straight to SRE.

anya: Great. Last ask: customer comms — we'll send a short note to customers on Friday explaining the 1.0.1 plan and expected timelines. @michael can you draft the technical blurb?

michael: Yep, I'll draft and share a WIP in #customer-commms by tomorrow morning.

anya: Perfect. Closing actions:
- sam: create triage board + link (30m)
- michael: draft technical blurb for customers (tomorrow AM)
- lee: reserve 2 devs + 1 SRE for hotfix window
- jordan: escalation contact
- anya: publish schedule and rubric after EOD approval

Thanks everyone :rocket:
